## $x_1$ seams between blocks (`layout: cubed`, `nb1` > 1) {#sec-ch03-x1seams}

Local symbols (flagged to the editor): $s$ an $x_1$ seam face shared by the block below ($\mathrm{B}$) and above
($\mathrm{T}$); $\mathbf F^{\mathrm{B}}_s$, $\mathbf F^{\mathrm{T}}_s$ the $x_1$ fluxes the two blocks compute there;
$p^{\mathrm{top}}$ the reference face pressure a block receives at its upper face.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What**: makes a column split into several $x_1$ blocks behave like one block: the hydrostatic reference scan is
relayed down the column, the reference ghost rows are the neighbour's interior rows, the switch-specific ghost rows
are exchanged, and across process seams the seam flux is averaged. **Switch**: YAML `distribute: {layout: cubed, nb1}`
with `nb1` > 1. **Default**: off (`nb1: 1`). **Requires**: `nghost` $\ge 3$ under `SNAP_WB_REF4`; blocks of one process
must run concurrently. **Order**: round-off agreement with one block, not bitwise. **Defining equation**:
@eq-ch03-x1seams-average.
:::

Only the `cubed` layout splits $x_1$ (@sec-ch03-layouts). The vertical schemes of @sec-ch05 are column operations: the
hydrostatic reference is a scan from the top of the column, and several switches read windows that reach past a block
edge. Four mechanisms make a split column match one block. (a) The reference scan is relayed from the top block down,
each block passing its bottom face value to the block below. (b) The reference ghost rows (`pref`, `dref`) are
overwritten with the neighbour's interior rows. (c) Under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` the plain-mean ghost cells and the
two face pressures past the seam are the neighbour's. (d) Across process seams only, the seam-face flux, face pressure
and reference flux are replaced by the mean of the two sides. Wall reconstructions and wall mirroring are gated on a
physical face, so they never act at a seam; column-wide EOS repairs gather the whole column.

### Derivation

**Single-valued seam flux.** Block B updates its top cell with $-A_s\mathbf F^{\mathrm{B}}_s/V$ and block T its bottom
cell with $+A_s\mathbf F^{\mathrm{T}}_s/V$. The column total changes at the seam by
$A_s(\mathbf F^{\mathrm{T}}_s - \mathbf F^{\mathrm{B}}_s)\Delta t$ per stage, zero only if the two agree. Both blocks
replace their value by

$$
\bar{\mathbf F}_s = \tfrac12\left(\mathbf F^{\mathrm{B}}_s + \mathbf F^{\mathrm{T}}_s\right),
$$ {#eq-ch03-x1seams-average}

and floating-point addition is commutative, so both hold the same bits and the sums telescope exactly across the seam.
@eq-ch03-x1seams-average is the seam average in `hydro_forward.cpp`, applied to the flux slab and, packed with it, the
face pressure and the reference flux `bflux1` ([`hydro_forward.cpp:425-499`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L425-L499)). It is applied only across
process seams; with mechanism (b) the two sides of an in-process seam already compute the same states, and the code
comment states that a same-process seam is not averaged.

**Reference relay.** The default reference is a scan of face pressures down from an anchor at the top of the column,
each cell adding its own hydrostatic drop. Split into blocks, each block needs as anchor the face value the scan has
reached at its upper face. The top block anchors itself; each other block takes $p^{\mathrm{top}}$ from the block above
and, after its own scan, passes its bottom face value down (`take_x1_anchor` and `pass_x1_anchor`,
[`hydro.cpp:518-579`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L518-L579)). The relay is serial from top to bottom, so every block's anchor equals the value the
one-block scan has at the same face, up to the order of the additions. The scan kernel itself is in @sec-ch05.

**Ghost rows.** A block's ghost rows of `pref`, `dref` computed locally from its ghost quadrature differ from the
owner's interior values; the code comment records about $10^2$ Pa near a wall. Replacing them by the neighbour's
interior rows, sent under `kWbGhostUpTag` and `kWbGhostDnTag`, makes the perturbation field identical on both
sides of the seam ([`hydro.cpp:581-640`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L581-L640)). Nothing in the derivation is truncated; the remaining differences from one block are round-off from
the order of operations. The executable check of these identities is not separate from the tests below.

### Numerical method

All four mechanisms run in every stage of a split column. The relay and the ghost-row exchange run inside
`_hydro_ref_x1`, when the well-balanced reconstruction builds its reference; the plain-mean ghost rows before it; the
seam average after the $x_1$ fluxes are computed and before the positivity limiter; the face-pressure ghost rows after
the average. A same-process neighbour is reached through an in-memory board, a remote one through the process group
(the parallelism, GPU and I/O chapter); `_x1_ghost_rows` packs $m$ rows from below the top face (up) and from above the bottom face (down) and
copies the neighbour's rows into its ghosts. The message tags are 0x7715 (relay), 0x7717 and 0x7718 (reference ghost
rows), 0x7720 and 0x7721 (seam flux), 0x7722 to 0x7725 (face-pressure and plain-mean ghost rows). EOS column repairs
call `gather_x1`, which joins the column's pieces bottom first. @fig-ch03-x1seams-relay shows a column of three blocks.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-x1seams-relay
#| fig-cap: "A column split into three $x_1$ blocks. Black arrows: the reference relay, top block to bottom block, one face value per seam. Purple arrows: each block's interior rows copied into the neighbour's ghost rows. At each seam face the two one-sided fluxes (orange) are replaced by their mean when the seam is between processes."
#| fig-alt: "Three stacked blocks with downward arrows at the seams, short arrows into hatched ghost rows, and paired flux arrows at each seam face."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch03.fig_x1seams_relay import make_fig
make_fig()
```

: Code map of the $x_1$ seams. {#tbl-ch03-x1seams-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-x1seams-code):

1. Setup refuses `SNAP_WB_REF4` (or `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`, which implies it) with `nghost` < 3, through
   `wb_ref4_enabled` ([`hydro.cpp:94-103`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L94-L103)).
2. In the stage, `phys_x1inner` and `phys_x1outer` gate the wall treatments ([`hydro_forward.cpp:240-262`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L240-L262));
   under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` the plain-mean ghost rows come from the neighbours with `_x1_ghost_rows`
   ([`hydro_forward.cpp:270-285`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L270-L285)).
3. `_hydro_ref_x1` takes the anchor from above, scans, passes its bottom face down, and swaps reference ghost rows
   with both neighbours using `kWbGhostDnTag` ([`hydro.cpp:502-640`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L502-L640)).
4. After the $x_1$ fluxes, a process seam is averaged with `kSeamFluxDnTag` ([`hydro_forward.cpp:425-499`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L425-L499)),
   then the face-pressure ghost rows past the seam are exchanged with `_x1_ghost_rows`
   ([`hydro_forward.cpp:501-508`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L501-L508)).

: Tests of the $x_1$ seams. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-x1seams-tests}

The reference cases are `local_blocks_restart_the_reference_at_the_seam` ([`test_pref_local_seam.cpp:99-143`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_pref_local_seam.cpp#L99-L143)) and
`in_process_split_matches_one_block_after_200_steps` ([`test_pref_local_seam.cpp:300-331`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_pref_local_seam.cpp#L300-L331)). The arms run one
gtest each with their environment through `seam_arm` ([`CMakeLists.txt:36-61`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/CMakeLists.txt#L36-L61)); the comparisons are in
`split_gap` and its callers ([`test_x1_seam_split.cpp:202-286`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp#L202-L286)). With `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT` the split
column is expected to differ and the test asserts only the $E+P$ drift of the split column ($10^{-13}$) and prints the
gap. CUDA twins of four arms are registered by `seam_arm` when CUDA is built ([`CMakeLists.txt:62-78`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/CMakeLists.txt#L62-L78)); the
`_mp` entries run on two ranks with `torchrun`. Their pass status at the pin was not run for this chapter (missing
evidence).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Blocks of one process in a split column must run concurrently; a block waits at most 5 minutes for its anchor.
- At most 16 blocks per process can exchange block messages.
- `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT` keeps a one-sided slope at block edges, so a split column differs from one block.
:::

A split column is not bitwise equal to one block; the tests use $10^{-13}$ and $10^{-12}$. Issue #250 recorded, before
the relay and ghost-row exchange existed, that $x_1$ splits on CPU with gloo differed from one rank by at most
$8.0\times10^{-15}$ relative while two GPUs with UCX were bitwise (`sources/gh__ISSUE_THREADS_138-250.md`, issue #250);
that measurement predates the pin and was not repeated here. The header comment of `test_pref_local_seam.cpp` still
says that `HydroImpl` restarts the scan in a second same-process block and that the test does not fix it, while the
assertions expect the fixed behaviour ([`test_pref_local_seam.cpp:1-15`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_pref_local_seam.cpp#L1-L15)). The switch combinations that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
